subject: Cardinal Analytics — evaluation playbook, recommended models & quant tradeoffs

Subject: Quick follow-up + sample prompts from today's demo

Thanks again for the demo this morning — we appreciated the throughput numbers and the live comparison. Per our conversation, attaching a representative prompt set and a short soak benchmark we'd like you to evaluate against two model families.

Key asks from our side:
- Could you run the attached prompts against the two candidate model families (open-coded and instruction-tuned variants) and share a short playbook of recommended model/quant combos?
- We're especially sensitive to hallucination in multi-turn diagnostics and latency under 250ms P95 for 512-token streams.
- Any quick thoughts on AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 for our expected 40–60 concurrent streams?

Attached: cardinal_prompt_set_v1.txt, quick_soak_spec.csv

Best,
Ayesha Khan

Cardinal Analytics

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + sample prompts from today's demo

Ayesha — thanks for sending the prompts and the soak spec. We're aligning resources to run two parallel eval tracks this week: one focused on end-to-end quality on your prompt set, the other focused on throughput/latency with realistic prefixes.

High level plan:
- Quality track: run instruction-tuned variants + Mistral- and Llama-family candidates at FP16 baseline, then 8-bit (GPTQ) and AWQ 4-bit quant to measure delta on hallucination and instruction-following.
- Throughput track: run streaming P95 tests at 512 tokens with target concurrency 40/60; include an FP8 experimental run to quantify raw token/sec gains and decode stability.

Deliverables by 2027-05-28:
- CSV of metrics (accuracy/regression, hallucination rate, token latency P50/P95)
- Short playbook with recommended model + quant profile and an estimated unit cost delta
- Notebook link and a short summary slide for your procurement team

Can we lock a 45-minute session on Friday for an interim readout? I can include Rishi (SE) and Ben (throughput SME).

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0142

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@cardinal.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + sample prompts from today's demo

Ayesha / team — quick technical note from the runs we started yesterday (short summary):

1) Candidate models we seeded: Mistral-Instruct-7B, Mistral-Instruct-14B, Llama2-13B-chat, Llama2-70B-chat. Baseline runs in FP16.

2) Quantization variants tested so far: GPTQ-8 (8-bit), AWQ-4 (4-bit blockwise), and an experimental FP8 path on the same kernels.

3) Early signals (on the sample prompt set):
- GPTQ-8: ~8–12% speedup vs FP16 on decode; minimal quality delta on single-turn instruction tasks. Multiturn diagnostics showed a small uptick in incorrect entity linking (~1.8% absolute).
- AWQ-4: biggest wins on memory footprint (reduces KV cache by ~55%) and throughput for 70B family on single-GPU config. Quality holds well on instruction-following, but we saw degradation on complex multi-step reasoning prompts (higher divergence on chain-of-thought style answers).
- FP8: raw token throughput is highest (20–30% vs FP16) but we observed unstable logits over very long contexts leading to occasional repetition artifacts; we'd mark FP8 as "experimental" for production without extra safeguards.

I'll upload the preliminary CSV to the drive link in the playbook and annotate which prompt IDs showed regressions. Will follow up with per-model recommendation and a pallet of fallback policies (e.g., detect divergence -> route to FP16 Llama2-70B-chat).

- Rishi (SE)

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cardinal.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + sample prompts from today's demo

Thanks for the rapid initial analysis. A few clarifying points from our side:

- The "multi-step reasoning" prompts are the highest priority to keep hallucination low — errors there materially impact our clinical reporting.
- Concurrency expectation for the pilot: 40 sustained streams but burst to 80 for daytime peaks. P95 latency target remains <=250ms for 512-token short-circuit streams.

Can you call out recommended production profile(s) for the pilot (model, quant profile, fallback rules, rough cost estimate)? Also include any instrumentation hooks we should enable to detect the regression cases you mentioned.

Tom
VP Product
Cardinal Analytics

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cardinal.ai>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@cardinal.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + sample prompts from today's demo — pilot profile and next steps

Tom / Ayesha — attached is the short playbook and the annotated CSV (drive link included). TL;DR recommendation for pilot:

Pilot production profile (recommended):
- Primary: Llama2-70B-chat @ AWQ-4 on dedicated GPUs (good balance: preserves instruction-following, large context KV savings).
- Fallback: Llama2-70B-chat @ FP16 (auto-route when divergence or hallucination signal > threshold).
- Secondary (cost-sensitive): Mistral-Instruct-14B @ GPTQ-8 for high-throughput routes where slightly higher hallucination tolerance exists (e.g., non-clinical summarization workloads).

Instrumentation and safeguards:
- Enable token-level perplexity monitoring and disagreement scoring (run candidate and compare top-3 logit agreement every 50 tokens).
- Echo-checks on entity mention lists (if extracted entity not present in input context, flag and route to FP16).
- Canary rollout: start at 10% traffic, run labelled prompt harness for regression detection, then 30%/60%/100%.

Cost/ops notes:
- AWQ-4 on 70B reduces memory per replica enabling 1.8x more replicas per GPU type we tested; estimated token-cost reduction ~38% vs FP16 for your workload mix.
- GPTQ-8 on Mistral-14B yields ~22% cost reduction vs FP16 but expect a slight trade in hallucination on multi-step prompts.
- FP8 gives the largest raw throughput improvements but requires a stabilization layer; recommend as an R&D path with a short pilot if you want raw latency tests.

Next steps I propose:
1) Card: sign the pilot statement of work (I'll send a DocuSign link today).
2) Technical kickoff with your infra + our SRE to map VPC/network requirements (schedule 60 mins).
3) Extended 7-day soak with your full prompt set and labelled anchors to validate clinical safety metrics.

I've attached: cardinal_benchmarks_summary.csv and the filled security questionnaire. If you want, we can move the cost estimates into a one-pager for procurement.

Available slots for the technical kickoff: Wed 6/2 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 6/3 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works?

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
